subject.title: fix(secrets): commit auth-stores before config to prevent half-migrated credentials

question: After the concurrent-edit rollback bug is fixed, should `openclaw-secops` accept the dependency-ordered `secrets apply` commit semantics, or require a broader journaled cross-store transaction design?
rationale: This PR changes which credential/config artifacts may persist after write faults in a CODEOWNERS-gated secrets path; automation can repair the lost-update bug, but only owners can accept the residual security semantics.

options.title: Fix rollback, then accept ordered mitigation
options.body: Repair the CAS rollback gap, preserve the targeted regression suite, and let secops approve the narrower ordered mitigation before merge.

options.title: Require journaled transaction design
options.body: Reject the ordered mitigation as insufficient and ask for a broader design that journals or otherwise coordinates config and all credential stores.

options.title: Ask for broader fault proof
options.body: Require additional proof for legacy `auth.json`/`.env` satellites or more production-like disk-fault timing before deciding the security boundary.

recommendation.title: Fix rollback, then accept ordered mitigation
recommendation.body: Repair the CAS rollback gap, preserve the targeted regression suite, and let secops approve the narrower ordered mitigation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The secrets apply flow history points to this owner as the best individual routing candidate, while final acceptance still belongs to the secops owner group.
